methodology: The study used ammonium persulfate (APS) oxidation to produce cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) from Sansevieria trifasciata fibers (STFs). The influences of APS concentration and oxidation temperature on the characteristics of CNCs were studied using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA).
research_objective: To study the effects of ammonium persulfate concentration and oxidation temperature on the characteristics of cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) produced from Sansevieria trifasciata fibers.

key_findings.finding: The APS oxidation process can successfully produce cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) from Sansevieria trifasciata fibers (STFs).
Optimum conditions for maximum crystallinity were achieved at an oxidation temperature of 70 ◦C, a reaction time of 16 h, and an APS concentration of 1.5 M.
The APS oxidation method can influence the properties of CNCs, including their crystallinity and thermal stability.
Increasing oxidation time generally increases the crystallinity of CNCs but decreases their thermal stability.
